name: Zk snarks

subjectOf.text: zk-SNARKs let a validator prove eligibility, meaning sufficient stake and a reputable history of cooperation, without revealing real-world identity or the specifics of staked assets.
subjectOf.abstract: enable validators to prove their eligibility—demonstrating sufficient stake and a reputable history of cooperative behavior—without revealing sensitive data such as their real-world identities or the precise details of their staked assets
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Cryptographic Foundations and Interdisciplinary Dimensions of the Secure Proof of Stake (SPoS) Conse (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5225296
scope_conditions: security rests on computational assumptions such as discrete logarithm or bilinear pairing hardness

subjectOf.text: By concealing validator identities while still verifying eligibility, zk-SNARKs mitigate the targeted attacks and coercion that identity exposure would otherwise invite.
subjectOf.abstract: The use of zk-SNARKs thus ensures that SPoS maintains a transparent yet private validator ecosystem, mitigating risks such as targeted attacks or coercion that could arise from identity exposure
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Cryptographic Foundations and Interdisciplinary Dimensions of the Secure Proof of Stake (SPoS) Conse (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5225296
